items.item: max_slot_wal_keep_size caps the WAL a replication slot may retain; past the cap, a slot that has fallen too far behind can no longer continue replication.

at.step: Reveal: the cap and its cost

items.item: Replication slots are guaranteed to retain all WAL entries a connector like Debezium needs, even during an outage.

at.step: Reveal: the slot's guarantee is the hazard

items.item: A heartbeat event, set via heartbeat.interval.ms, advances a slot's position on a table with few relevant updates.

at.step: Reveal: the cap and its cost

items.item: The guarantee that protects the pipeline from data loss is the same guarantee that fills the disk once the pipeline stops.

at.step: Reveal: the slot's guarantee is the hazard

items.item: A cap bounds the slot's growth at the cost of a forced re-snapshot once crossed, not a free fix.

at.step: Reveal: the cap and its cost

items.item: A new consumer needs the table's state and then every change after it, without a gap or an overlap between the two.

at.step: Reveal: snapshot and stream, handed over without a gap

items.item: A deleted row and a schema change are each events the merge must be told how to apply, not events it can infer.
A stalled compaction stalls the merge, which stalls the slot, which grows the source's own log — the interaction this design itself creates.

at.step: Reveal: compaction stalls, and the slot grows with it

items.item: A code leak in the connector wouldn't track as cleanly with exactly when the connector stopped and resumed as slot retention does.

at.step: Predict: what did the design fail to say about the slot?

items.item: Raising the cap doesn't remove the trade this design names; it only delays the choice between the source's disk and a forced re-snapshot.

at.step: Prove it: a second slot, already most of the way to its cap

items.item: This topic leaves out logical decoding, replication-slot and WAL internals, Debezium and Kafka Connect mechanics, table-format MOR internals, and the exactly-once argument itself.
Log-based CDC and watermark-based incremental snapshots are established practice, not an emerging technique.
This topic gives the shop its CDC design; the next design is a lakehouse with concurrent writers and time travel, once several writers touch the same table.
